content.text:
The idea is sound and fits mise’s bootstrap model. I’d accept it, but the implementation is broader than adding `optional = true`.

The [discussion](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/12954) proposes:

```toml
"brew-cask:ghostty" = { os = "macos", optional = true }
```

with interactive selection and explicit inclusion flags. There are currently no replies or reactions.

Key findings:

- The table-form package schema is the right extension point. It already carries `version`, `os`, `adopt`, and `state`; unknown fields are rejected today. See [src/system/mod.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/3abd/mise/src/system/mod.rs:142).
- Optionality must travel on `PackageRequest`, where merged declarations become executable package requests. See [src/system/mod.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/3abd/mise/src/system/mod.rs:630).
- Both `mise bootstrap` and `mise bootstrap packages apply` use the same package driver, so most selection logic can be shared. See [src/cli/system/install.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/3abd/mise/src/cli/system/install.rs:65) and [src/cli/bootstrap.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/3abd/mise/src/cli/bootstrap.rs:1468).
- Today, unattended execution installs missing packages automatically; `--yes` only suppresses confirmation. Optional packages therefore need explicit filtering before the driver’s mutation step. See [src/cli/system/driver.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/3abd/mise/src/cli/system/driver.rs:128).
- Status, plans, `doctor`, and the `mise install` missing-package hint currently treat every missing `state = "present"` package as drift. These must exclude missing optional packages. See [src/cli/system/status.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/3abd/mise/src/cli/system/status.rs:77), [src/system/resources.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/3abd/mise/src/system/resources.rs:660), and [src/cli/install.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/3abd/mise/src/cli/install.rs:233).
- OCI builds consume the same declarations non-interactively, so optional packages should be omitted by default there too. See [src/cli/oci/common.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/3abd/mise/src/cli/oci/common.rs:65).

Recommended semantics:

- Missing required package: drift; install normally.
- Missing optional package: acceptable state; prompt only in an attended interactive apply.
- `--yes` or non-interactive execution: skip missing optionals.
- `--with-optional`: include every applicable optional package.
- `--optional`: accept full `manager:package` identifiers. Bare names such as `firefox` become ambiguous across managers.
- Explicit positional packages continue to install normally.
- An already-installed optional remains managed: status reports it installed, upgrade may upgrade it, and version mismatch/repair can converge it.
- Optional declarations continue protecting packages from `prune`.
- Reject `optional = true` combined with `state = "absent"` as contradictory.
- Dry-run should report optional packages as skipped/available unless inclusion was explicitly requested.

For interaction, mise already depends on a multiselect component used by `mise upgrade`. A single multiselect of applicable missing optionals would be cleaner than three separate yes/no prompts, especially as optional lists grow.

Overall: good feature, probably a medium-sized `feat(bootstrap)` change. The main risk is implementing apply-time selection while leaving status, plans, doctor, hints, or OCI claiming the package is still required. No workspace changes were made.

 Other built-in managers currently support only the default `state = "present"`.
+
+Set `optional = true` for software that mise should offer during an interactive
+bootstrap without requiring on every machine. Missing optional packages are not
+reported as drift by `status --missing`, `bootstrap plan`, `mise doctor`, or the
+system-package hint printed by `mise install`. An attended `mise bootstrap` or
+`mise bootstrap packages apply` shows a multiselect for missing optional packages.
+Unattended runs, `--yes`, and dry runs skip them unless `--with-optional` is passed:
+
+```sh
+mise bootstrap --with-optional --yes
+mise bootstrap packages apply --with-optional --yes
+```
+
+To install only one optional package without a prompt, name it explicitly, for
+example `mise bootstrap packages apply brew-cask:ghostty --yes`. Once installed,
+an optional package remains managed: apply can repair it or enforce a supported
+version pin, upgrade includes it, and prune treats its declaration as in use.
